title: Anthropic measures how agents influence expert decisions
dek: A randomized study of professional analysts reveals strong influence on four methodological decisions.
evidence: Primary controlled experiment; limited sample and task
takeaway: A final human sign-off does not necessarily mean the analyst independently selected the methods that determine the result.

sections.title: Context

bullets.detail: An analyst may approve a correct computation while accepting an agent's unexamined choice of metric, peer group or treatment definition.

paragraphs: Why human approval can mislead: An analyst may approve a correct computation while accepting an agent's unexamined choice of metric, peer group or treatment definition.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: Anthropic asked 50 experienced analysts to study a fictional farm program using Claude Code. Hidden random assignments made the agent advocate one of two reasonable options for each of four analytic decisions.
Four choices determined the method; a fifth was the final program recommendation. Claude was instructed to argue honestly from the available data, not fabricate evidence.

paragraphs: Randomized agent preferences: Anthropic asked 50 experienced analysts to study a fictional farm program using Claude Code. Hidden random assignments made the agent advocate one of two reasonable options for each of four analytic decisions.
Five decisions in total: Four choices determined the method; a fifth was the final program recommendation. Claude was instructed to argue honestly from the available data, not fabricate evidence.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.detail: Analysts followed their agent's assigned lean across four methodological choices: 92% outcome, 82% comparison, 81% population and 90% weighting.
54% recommended rollout when the agent favored it, versus 36% when it opposed it. The 11 participants without an agent chose that condition themselves, so AI-versus-no-AI benefit is not randomized.
Preferences were deliberately strengthened in a single-task experiment with one model; 86% is not a general real-world rate.

paragraphs: 86% method agreement: Analysts followed their agent's assigned lean across four methodological choices: 92% outcome, 82% comparison, 81% population and 90% weighting.

Weaker final influence: 54% recommended rollout when the agent favored it, versus 36% when it opposed it. The 11 participants without an agent chose that condition themselves, so AI-versus-no-AI benefit is not randomized.
Limit: Preferences were deliberately strengthened in a single-task experiment with one model; 86% is not a general real-world rate.

sections.title: Why it matters

bullets.detail: Ask analysts to record outcome definitions and comparison methods before the agent recommends one.
Evaluate the provenance of methodology changes and counterfactual results, even when the calculations are correct.

paragraphs: Precommit key assumptions: Ask analysts to record outcome definitions and comparison methods before the agent recommends one.
